subject: Geography
description: Atmospheric layers, monsoons, climate classification, pressure belts

questions.stem: The layer of the atmosphere closest to the Earth's surface, in which WEATHER phenomena (clouds, rain) occur, is:
questions.explanation: Troposphere: 0–12 km (varies with latitude), contains ~75% of atmospheric mass and essentially all water vapour. Temperature decreases with height (lapse rate ~6.5 °C/km). Above it lies the stratosphere (with the ozone layer).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Indian SOUTH-WEST monsoon normally arrives in Kerala around:
questions.explanation: Climatological onset at Kerala coast: 1 June (±a few days). IMD uses Kerala onset as the official start. The monsoon then advances northward — Mumbai by ~10 June, Delhi by ~29 June, full coverage by mid-July.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The OZONE layer — which absorbs most of the Sun's harmful UV-B radiation — is located primarily in the:
questions.explanation: Stratospheric ozone lies ~15-35 km up. Different from tropospheric ozone (ground-level pollutant). Montreal Protocol (1987) regulates CFCs that deplete it; the Antarctic 'ozone hole' appears each spring.

questions.stem: Match the LATITUDINAL pressure belt with its characteristic. A. Equatorial low (Doldrums).  B. Sub-tropical high (Horse latitudes).  C. Sub-polar low.  D. Polar high. List-II: 1. Calm region of descending air around 30° N/S — deserts common here. 2. Rising warm moist air near equator — heavy rainfall. 3. Cold descending air at the poles. 4. Convergence of westerlies and polar easterlies around 60° N/S.
questions.explanation: Equatorial low — rising moist air → ITCZ, rainforests. Sub-tropical high (30°) — descending dry air → Sahara, Thar, Atacama. Sub-polar low (60°) — convergence zone → frontal storms. Polar high — extreme cold dense descending air.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Consider the following about EL NIÑO. 1. It is a warming of surface waters in the EASTERN equatorial Pacific (off Peru). 2. It typically WEAKENS the Indian summer monsoon, causing below-normal rainfall in India. 3. It occurs roughly every 2-7 years. 4. Its opposite phase — cooling of eastern Pacific surface waters — is called La Niña. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: All four correct. El Niño + Southern Oscillation (ENSO) = coupled ocean-atmosphere phenomenon. El Niño reduces the pressure gradient that drives the Indian SW monsoon → weaker monsoon (not all El Niño years mean drought — neutral factors like IOD matter too). La Niña usually aids the Indian monsoon.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Which place in India receives the HIGHEST average annual rainfall?
questions.explanation: Mawsynram currently records the highest annual average (~11,872 mm). Cherrapunji is close second and held the record historically. Both benefit from funnel-shaped Khasi hills trapping SW monsoon moisture. Agumbe is sometimes called 'the Cherrapunji of the South'.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The WESTERLIES that bring winter rainfall to north-western India (especially Punjab, Haryana, western UP) are called:
questions.explanation: Western Disturbances — extra-tropical low-pressure systems originating in the Mediterranean / Caspian and travelling east on sub-tropical westerlies. They bring December–February rain/snowfall that is critical for rabi (wheat) crops. Loo is hot, dry summer wind; mango showers are March-April convective showers in Kerala/Karnataka.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Which hot, dry local wind blows across the Indo-Gangetic Plain during May–June afternoons and is a major cause of heat-stroke fatalities in northern India?

options.option_text: Kalbaisakhi — violent pre-monsoon squalls over Bengal
Loo — scorching westerly wind over the northern plains
Mango showers — pre-monsoon convective rain over Kerala
Norwester — severe thunderstorms active over the northeast

questions.explanation: The Loo is a hot, dry, dust-laden westerly wind that blows over Punjab, Haryana, UP, and Rajasthan during May–June and causes serious heat-stroke conditions. Kalbaisakhi (Nor'westers) are violent pre-monsoon thunderstorms over West Bengal and Assam — they are wet and gusty, not dry heat winds.

questions.stem: The NORTH-EAST monsoon, which develops after the south-west monsoon retreats, delivers the bulk of its rainfall to which coastal stretch of India during October–December?

options.option_text: Konkan coast (Maharashtra) during the rabi crop season
Malabar coast (Kerala) during the peak summer harvest
Odisha coast (Chilika belt) during the early winter months

questions.explanation: The north-east monsoon picks up moisture crossing the Bay of Bengal and deposits heavy rainfall on the Coromandel coast — Chennai receives about 60% of its annual rain during this period. The Konkan and Malabar coasts are windward to the south-west monsoon, not the north-east monsoon.

questions.stem: Pre-monsoon convective showers in Kerala and coastal Karnataka (April–May), locally called 'Mango showers', earn that name primarily because they:

options.option_text: Signal the withdrawal of the north-east monsoon from Tamil Nadu
Coincide with and assist the ripening of mango crop in the region
Initiate the flowering season of paddy across the Deccan Plateau
Trigger the onset of the south-west monsoon over the Arabian Sea

questions.explanation: Mango showers are localised convective rains in April–May that help mango trees ripen their fruit before the main south-west monsoon arrives — hence the name. They also benefit coffee and sandalwood crops. They have no causal link to paddy flowering on the Deccan or to monsoon onset timing over the Arabian Sea.

questions.stem: During a 'BREAK IN MONSOON', when the monsoon trough shifts to the Himalayan foothills, the most characteristic weather pattern that develops is:

options.option_text: Heavy rainfall spreading uniformly across the Deccan and Rajasthan
Heavy rain in hill states and foothills; dry spell over the main plains
Complete cessation of rainfall across the entire Indian subcontinent
Cyclonic storms intensifying over the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea

questions.explanation: When the monsoon trough shifts northward during a break, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, and the northeast receive intense orographic rainfall while central and peninsular plains experience a dry spell. The monsoon is not withdrawn — it is spatially redistributed. Cyclonic storms are a separate monsoon-season phenomenon, not a consequence of the break.

questions.stem: The ITCZ (Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone) migrates seasonally. Its pronounced northward shift over the Indian subcontinent during summer is the primary driver of which phenomenon?

options.option_text: Onset of western disturbances that bring winter rain to Punjab
Onset and progressive north-westward advance of the south-west monsoon
Formation of the Siberian High that controls Indian winter climate
Triggering of the north-east monsoon over Tamil Nadu in October

questions.explanation: The south-west monsoon is effectively the ITCZ displaced far northward over South Asia by intense continental heating. As the ITCZ migrates north, converging trade winds bring the monsoon onset over Kerala and advance it toward north-west India. Western disturbances are extra-tropical Mediterranean systems unrelated to ITCZ migration; the Siberian High is a winter cold-air phenomenon.

questions.stem: The 'MASCARENE HIGH' — a semi-permanent subtropical anticyclone over the southern Indian Ocean — drives the Indian summer monsoon primarily because it:

options.option_text: Supplies cold, dry polar air that cools the Tibetan Plateau in summer
Acts as the source region for the cross-equatorial south-west monsoon flow
Generates western disturbances that merge with the monsoon trough
Weakens the Somali Jet, delaying the south-west monsoon over Kerala

questions.explanation: The Mascarene High (centred near Mauritius/Madagascar, ~20°–30°S) drives south-east trade winds northward toward the equator. Crossing the equator near the Somali coast, the Coriolis effect deflects them rightward into the south-westerlies — the south-west monsoon current. The Mascarene High actually energises the Somali Jet, not weakens it. Western disturbances originate over the Mediterranean/Caspian region and are unrelated to this high.

questions.stem: The 'THERMAL EQUATOR' — the belt of highest mean surface temperature — does not coincide with the geographic equator. During the Northern Hemisphere summer, it shifts to approximately:

options.option_text: 5°N latitude, staying close to the geographic equatorial rain belt
20°N–25°N latitude, deep into the Northern Hemisphere land masses
10°S latitude, following the Southern Ocean temperature patterns
30°N latitude, aligning with the subtropical high-pressure belt

questions.explanation: The thermal equator migrates toward the hemisphere with more land mass because continents heat faster than oceans. In Northern Hemisphere summer, intense heating over the Sahara, Arabian Peninsula, and the Thar Desert pulls the thermal equator northward to ~20°N–25°N, generating the continental heat low that draws in the south-west monsoon. 5°N is too close to the geographic equator; 30°N corresponds to subtropical anticyclones — the opposite of heat lows.
